The third surah is Surah al-Nas: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, (1) the King of mankind, (2) the God of mankind, (3) from the evil of the sneaking whisperer, (4) who whispers in the breasts of mankind, (5) of jinn and of mankind.﴾ [al-Nas 1-6].

﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾ — He is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He is the Lord of mankind and of others: the Lord of mankind, the Lord of the angels, the Lord of the jinn, the Lord of the heavens, the Lord of the earth, the Lord of the sun, the Lord of the moon, the Lord of everything. But for the context, He specified mankind.

﴿The King of mankind﴾ means: the King who holds supreme authority over mankind and complete control is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿The God of mankind﴾ means: their object of worship and the one they worship. The one truly worthy of worship, whom hearts devote themselves to, love and glorify, is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿from the evil of the sneaking whisperer (4) who whispers in the breasts of mankind (5) of jinn and of mankind﴾.

﴿al-Waswas (the whisperer)﴾: The scholars said it is a verbal noun used in the sense of the active participle, i.e., the one who whispers (al-muwaswis). Waswasah (whispering) is what is cast into the heart of thoughts, delusions and imaginings that have no reality.

﴿al-Khannas (the sneaking one)﴾: the one who withdraws, retreats, flees and turns back when the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is made. This is Satan. For this reason, "When the caller to prayer calls the adhan, Satan turns away and flees, and he has a loud fart from the intensity of what he finds of distress; when the adhan finishes, he returns"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (608), and the wording is his, and Muslim (389/19), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns his back and has a loud fart so that he does not hear the call to prayer; when the call ends, he comes back..." to the end of the hadith.]], we ask Allah for well-being. And for this reason it came in a report: "When the ghouls appear, hasten to the adhan"[[Narrated by Ahmad (14277) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. The ghouls (al-ghilan) are the devils that appear to the traveller on his journey, as if they were terrifying things or an enemy or the like; when a person says Allahu akbar, they depart. So His words, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿al-Khannas﴾ mean the one who withdraws, i.e., departs, turns back, flees and is humiliated before the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

As for His words ﴿of jinn and of mankind﴾, meaning that the whispering may come from the jinn and may come from the children of Adam. As for the whispering of the jinn, it is evident, since it flows through the son of Adam as blood flows. As for the whispering of mankind, how many are those who come to a person, inspiring him with evil and adorning it in his heart until this speech takes hold of his mind and he turns toward it.

These three surahs[[i.e., Surah al-Ikhlas, Surah al-Falaq and Surah al-Nas.]] — "When the Prophet ﷺ went to his bed, he would blow into his palms, rub them over his face and whatever part of his body he could reach"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5017) from the hadith of Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]], and "he sometimes recited them after the five prayers"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2903) with his chain from Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to recite the two protective surahs at the end of every prayer.]]. So a person should be careful to follow the Sunnah in reciting them in their proper places, as came from the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family. With this we conclude the last juz' of the Quran, which is Juz' 'Amma (Juz' al-Naba').
